newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AHK to focus on European cargo routes.
newsitem.headline: AHK to focus on European cargo routes.

text.p: AHK Air Hong Kong Ltd, which is handing back its trans-Pacific service to parent company Cathay Pacific, plans to increase capacity on European and Japanese destinations instead, AHK's chief operating officer Kenny Tang told Reuters.
Tang said he was not ruling out the possibility of launching new European destinations "but where, I have no idea yet."

Nine months after AHK took over Chicago, Cathay Pacific announced Monday that it was planning to restart flying to O'Hare from June as part of its New York freighter service. One of Cathay's two Boeing 747-400 freighters will be used which are more efficient than AHK's 747-200 aircraft, Cathay said. AHK is 75 percent owned by Hong Kong's de facto flag carrier.

Pilot sources, who asked not to be identified because of poor industrial relations with management, said AHK's Chicago service flopped because of problems with a controversial "cut price" company called Aircrew Services Limited (ASL) set up by Cathay to recuit cargo pilots for both Cathay and AHK which offers lower pay rates and reduced conditions enjoyed by Cathay passenger pilots.
Cathay has said ASL makes the cost structure of the freighter operation competitive.

Tang said the switch was mainly due to the higher efficiency of the 747-400 but also said AHK had not been able to recruit the required number of U.S.-based crew to enable the service to expand to three times weekly as envisaged. He said concentration on routes to Europe would mean a change in the way AHK's pilots work but no job cuts.
Tang described the trans-Pacific route as "marginal" because of heavy competition and fluctuating yields.

"On the other hand, the European market is more stable. There are a lot of carriers but compared to the U.S. it is less fluctuating so it makes sense to deploy our capacity into Europe and Japan to give us a stable return," Tang said.
AHK has already said it expects to increase services to Dubai, Brussels and Manchester to a maximum five frequencies a week by next month because of strong demand.
Seoul, which had been raised in the last bilateral talks between Hong Kong and the South Korean governments also remained a possibility but more discussions are needed, Tang added.
AHK has just increased frequency from Hong Kong to Osaka to three times weekly and another possibility is additional frequencies there too, Tang added.

News of the new route came as Cathay's annual report was published. The financial results of AHK are not released but the annual report said the cargo carrier made a small loss for the year. Fuel prices increased significantly but cost saving measures introduced in earlier years helped in a difficult revenue market.

The report added that AHK is now placed in a very competitive position to capitalise on market opportunities in 1997 and beyond. Management is confident of future prospects, it added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
